A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpargeAttn/SpargeAttention research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable. Existing material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including Appendices A.1–A.3; v3 adds A.4.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-quality measurements, attention and generation timings, permutation and self-similarity ablations, and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds Open-Sora-Plan results, video examples, and CogvideoX sparsity analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same operations after accounting for line numbering. Selective token compression, warp-level filtering, SageAttention integration, Hilbert permutation, and calibration remain unchanged. The new selective/fix-block terminology and explicit mean in the similarity expression clarify behavior already described in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText, LongBench, InfiniteBench En.MC, Needle-in-a-Haystack, open-sora video prompts, and COCO annotations for the same tasks. Open-Sora-Plan adds a model within the retained text-to-video evaluation; no distinct dataset, domain, or task requirement is introduced.

E2.justification: Full Attention, MInference, FlexPrefill, and the kernel-comparison methods remain in their corresponding existing comparisons. The new Open-Sora-Plan experiment uses the already established Full Attention comparator. FlexPrefill's updated author citation does not introduce a different baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds an Open-Sora-Plan evaluation at 38K tokens with calibration thresholds l1=0.03 and l2=0.035. Appendix A.4 introduces sparsity profiling across layers, heads, denoising timesteps, and ten prompts. Settings for the retained experiments, including the five-prompt permutation ablation, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.4 systematically investigates where sparsity occurs across CogvideoX layers, heads, denoising timesteps, and prompts, substantially extending the diagnostic analyses beyond the existing component ablations. Figures 6 and 12 also add qualitative video comparisons. The earlier permutation, self-similarity, filtering-stage, and sequence-length analyses are retained.

E5.justification: No new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests are reported. Appendix A.2 retains its threshold-based case selection. The new sparsity plots show descriptive averages and profiles rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing numerical table entries and matched kernel/NIAH plots are retained. Table 1 adds Open-Sora-Plan results: SpargeAttn reports 34% sparsity and 393s latency versus Full Attention's 629s, with VQA-a 77.59 versus 81.40 and VQA-t 76.91 versus 80.60. New figures add video examples and findings of heterogeneous layer/head sparsity and increasing sparsity across denoising steps.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 changes CosSim(X) from XX^T/|max(XX^T)| to the mean of that expression. This corrects the mathematical specification to a scalar consistent with the averaging already described in v2. The mask definitions and online-softmax derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit claim that SpargeAttn is the first sparse attention method to accelerate language, image, and video models without compromising accuracy. The universality, training-free operation, two-stage filtering, and acceleration claims were already present; adding training-free to the title does not introduce that claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets layer/head sparsity variation as evidence that different hyperparameters are necessary for different layers and heads. Earlier explanations concerning Hilbert locality and sparse attention focusing LLMs on relevant information remain. No substantive new limitation qualifies the retained no-metric-loss claims.

D1.justification: Calibration thresholds for Open-Sora-Plan are newly documented. Conversely, the kernel-speed caption loses the RTX4090 identification and explanations of the +Sage/+Sage2 variants present in v2 Figure 9. CUDA implementation information, appendix block sizes, and the code-access and SageAttention2 implementation note are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including Sparse VideoGen/2, SageAttention2++/3, Open-Sora-Plan, and additional quantization work, alongside the explicit first-across-model-domains claim. The related-work taxonomy and comparisons remain largely unchanged. FlexPrefill's author correction and SageAttention2's publication update concern retained works.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and author/publication information, explains selective and fix blocks, makes localized wording corrections, and adds acknowledgments, an impact statement, and Appendix A.4. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained; this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: New Figures 6, 12, and 14–17 substantially expand the visual presentation with video galleries and sparsity plots, including a full layer-by-head panel grid. Table 1 gains an Open-Sora-Plan block. Existing figures, Algorithm 1, and tables are relocated or resized, and Tables 8–9 move their captions below the tables; retained graphics are matched rather than treated as deleted.

improvement.justification: The added Open-Sora-Plan evaluation and CogvideoX sparsity profiles provide useful additional evidence, while the scalar similarity correction improves internal consistency. These gains modestly outweigh the loss of the kernel plot's hardware annotation. The improvement remains limited: the retained no-metric-loss claim needs qualification because the new Open-Sora-Plan results show lower VQA scores alongside lower latency.
